explanation: Fires on a later subword piece that completes a multi-token name or word (place names like Black|pool, Midloth|ian, En|field; brand/product names; code identifiers like set|up, Sw|agger; M|ale). Also fires on some code tokens like 'self' and format strings. Common short function words fire only weakly. No single shared meaning beyond 'continuation of a fragmented word or name'.

Fires on a word-internal subword piece in the middle of a long technical/medical word, especially Greek/Latin roots like -oc- (leukocytosis, Streptococcus, homocysteine), per|ic|ardium, and pieces of words in Scandinavian/German/Esperanto text (produ|k|ter, k|ropp, Jahr|z|ehnten). Firing is strongest on mid-word consonant-heavy fragments of scientific terms; whole common words do not fire.

Mixed: fires on 'here' in 'click here', on word endings that complete a fragmented word (un-metabol|ized, I|LL|INOIS, Ingegä|rd), and on idiom completions (changed my mind, don't mean, no more, not wanted). No clear common thread; weak firing is scattered.

Fires on word-initial or word-internal subword fragments of rare/foreign words and names (ALBU|QU|ERQUE, Lem|ait|re, Gal|atzan, Intracerebro|vent|ricular, den|ials), plus compiler flag pieces after '-' ('-f' in -fno-exceptions) and tokens in Spanish/French/Italian/German text. Seems to respond to the start of a multi-piece word whose completion is uncertain; ordinary English words fire weakly.

Fires on a middle or later subword piece of long technical/scientific or capitalized words (monon|uclear, tetra|hydro|biopterin, phosph|or, retic|ulum, MEM|OR|ANDUM, HON|EST|Y, SHO|ES, DTD). Strongest when the token is part of a long domain-specific compound split into several pieces; function words fire only weakly.

Fires on a function word (by, of, on, after, before, for, not, 're, n't) that comes right after a verb/noun phrase and opens a complement saying how/why something happens, especially 'concluded by', 'responds by', 'protects itself by', 'chances of', 'planning on', 'hard time'. Firing depends on the preceding verb or noun taking that preposition; prepositions in other uses fire weakly.

Fires on a word in formal/academic or legal writing that links a head noun or verb to its complement: 'effect(s)' in 'investigated the effects of', 'of'/'in' after 'predictors', 'defects', 'components', 'rights in', 'capacity as', 'in part', 'affecting', 'relating'. Mainly the token where a relational phrase is continued in an abstract or license boilerplate; casual text fires weakly.

Fires on a colon (or colon-like separator) inside a structured notation: times (03:13 PM, 15:12), docket/case numbers (1:08-CV), math function signatures (f: X -> R), tag URIs, and labels. Strongest for the colon in clock times and 'f:\mathbb' math; colons introducing prose (Italian: "...") and semicolons fire weaker.

Fires on file names or paths referenced in software license headers and code, especially 'LICENSE' / 'license' file references ("see the LICENSE file", LICENSE_1_0.txt, /licenses/LICENSE-2.0) and version digits there; also README, other file names in paths (test.html, store.php). Strongest in license boilerplate pointing to an accompanying file.

Fires on a variety of content and function tokens early in a new sentence or clause in casual or news prose (Just do, To activate, By the, so, much better) with no clear shared feature; also fires on some code and non-English tokens. Hard to predict.

Fires on 'of' in 'what kind of', 'what sort of', 'what type of', 'which one of', and more weakly on the noun or adjective right after an interrogative 'what'/'which' (what name, what other, what option, to what extent). Requires an interrogative determiner context; ordinary 'of' does not fire.

Fires on programming-concept vocabulary and code identifier pieces in programming discussions and code: low-level, black-box, overload, implementor, unprotected, dependency injection, backwards compatibility, functional, '//' comments, C++ attribute names. Responds to software-engineering jargon tokens; plain prose fires near zero.

Mixed: fires on 'carried' in 'a study was carried out', 'file' in 'No such file or directory', and on fragments inside tool/package names and log lines (osm2|p|grouting, p2|c, D|/dalvikvm, amd6|4). No single concept connects these.

Fires on specific named entities and fixed boilerplate tokens: '@implementation' in Objective-C files, '/local' in /usr/local paths, 'Latter' in Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Hamas/Palestinians/hostage in Middle-East conflict news, license disclaimer words (PROFITS, FITNESS), CDN names. Several unrelated recurring strings.

Fires on the leading indentation whitespace token at the start of the first statement inside a just-opened function or block body in code (after '{' and newline), strongest for the first line of a function body in JS/TS. Also weakly on newline tokens after a closing comment or block. Indentation deeper in a body fires less.

Fires on a wide assortment of tokens: word continuations (ass|istance, F|int|ech, Pill|Cam), citation-tag pieces (@B7-s|ensors), verbs after 'how to', particles after verbs (cheated on, back|dated). No coherent pattern.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word that begins a word with a Latin/Greek medical or technical stem, especially 'creat' (creatinine), 'am' (amniotomy, amorphous), 'ym' (honeymoon, readymade), plus 'reproductive', 'athletic', 'ser'(ine), and initial capital letters/pieces (M|DF, R|ömstedt, r|ingleader). Strongest in biomedical text on word-initial fragments.

Fires on byte-fragment tokens of multibyte UTF-8 characters (shown as �) in CJK, Hindi, or emoji text, i.e. the first byte piece of a character split across tokens; strongest on Devanagari and broken-encoding text. Normal ASCII tokens barely fire.

Fires on a wide range of tokens (units like Hz/mg/degrees, 'the', 'source', 'fig', 'these', reference anchors) with no evident shared trigger; perhaps tokens that complete a noun phrase after a number or determiner, but examples are too diverse.

Fires on function words and nouns in comparative/quantity or generalization contexts in prose (more and more importance, more attention, more women, far less, most people, more likely ... to, as a source), i.e. the token right after a quantifier or within a 'more/less X' construction; also on some unrelated code tokens (.get). Moderately coherent around quantity/comparison.

Fires on a head noun that names what kind of thing an entity is, in definitional or descriptive phrases: Japanese 技術/存在/品, 'mollusk', 'antibody', 'company', 'politician', 'footballer', 'racing driver', 'camera', 'cooler', 'License' in (the "License"). Strongest on the category noun after a descriptive lead-in ("is a Pakistani politician").
